title: Direct observation of flat bands in near-magic-angle twisted bilayer CVD graphene
authors: Gianluigi Baiardi, Alex Boschi, Giulia Piccinini, Vaidotas Mišeikis, Lorenzo Cavicchi, Aaron Bostwick, Chris Jozwiak, Eli Rotenberg, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Marco Polini, Fabio Beltram, Antonio Rossi, Stiven Forti, Sergio Pezzini, Camilla Coletti
abstract: Advances in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth have driven graphene crystal quality to unprecedented levels, yet it is still unknown whether this route can realize the fragile flat-band and correlated states of the magic-angle (MA) twisted bilayer graphene (TBG). Here, we report on the experimental observation by room-temperature nano-angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) of flat bands in a TBG sample close to the MA, assembled via a grow-and-stack protocol based on low-pressure CVD of graphene on copper. Our study indicates electronic bands fully comparable to those measured in exfoliation-based samples and determines the size of the largest near-MA domain to be compatible with electronic transport experiments, motivating further experiments on flat band physics in CVD-graphene.
summary: This work reports the direct experimental observation of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene grown via CVD, overcoming a major hurdle in scaling up MATBG research. By using nano-ARPES, the authors confirmed that CVD-grown samples exhibit electronic properties comparable to exfoliated samples. This validates CVD as a viable platform for studying strongly correlated physics in moiré materials.
main_problem: The primary goal was to determine if the fragile flat-band and correlated electronic states characteristic of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) could be realized using scalable, large-area growth methods like Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD).
main_result: The study successfully observed electronic bands in CVD-grown TBG that are comparable to those measured in exfoliated samples, confirming the potential for scalable moiré materials hosting flat bands.
method: The research employed room-temperature nano-Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) on CVD-assembled TBG domains, supplemented by STM and advanced data fitting techniques.
model_or_system: The physical system is Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) formed by stacking CVD-grown graphene layers near the magic angle. The electronic structure is analyzed using models derived from the moiré superlattice potential.
key_observables: Flat-band dispersion, gap opening near the Fermi level, Moiré lattice parameter (12.9 nm), and the relaxation length of the near-MA configuration.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($\sim 1.11^\circ$), doping shift ($> 100$ meV), and the domain size compatible with transport experiments.
main_assumptions: The observed p-doping shift is attributed to synchrotron-radiation-induced photodoping, and the analysis relies on fitting EDCs with Lorentzian/Voigt lineshapes.
figures_summary: Figures show STM imaging of the moiré superlattice, ARPES-revealed electronic dispersion with flat bands, and position-resolved EDC fitting used to map the electronic configuration across the domain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the experimental feasibility of CVD-grown MATBG, through quantitative ARPES measurements confirming flat bands, to detailed analysis mapping domain homogeneity and electronic structure.
why_interesting: The realization of correlated electronic states in a scalable, solid-state platform like CVD graphene is crucial for studying strongly correlated electron physics outside of highly controlled, small-sample environments.
